title: Default CORS configuration reflects arbitrary origins with credentials
impact: Cross-origin reads are theoretically possible from any site; current session cookie is SameSite=lax, which blocks cross-site fetch, so impact is deployment-dependent (e.g., WEBUI_AUTH_COOKIE_SAME_SITE=none).
preconditions: Browser session cookie sent cross-site (SameSite=none) or token available to attacker origin.

evidence.note: OPTIONS /api/v1/auths/signin with Origin: https://evil.example returns ACAO echo + ACAC true

fix_suggestion: Do not reflect arbitrary origins when allow_credentials=true; require explicit CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN allowlist in production.
note: Documented as hardening note, not submitted as a vulnerability.

title: No framing protection on UI (clickjacking surface)
impact: UI can be framed by third-party sites; UI actions could be clickjacked. Requires user interaction and a plausible overlay.
preconditions: Victim visits attacker page framing the instance.
fix_suggestion: Add X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN or CSP frame-ancestors 'self'.
